principle.name: Separate UI Logic from Business Logic
principle.description: Maintain clean separation between Tkinter UI code and AutoCAD operations
principle.rationale: Improves maintainability, testability, and reusability of code components

example.bad: # Bad: Mixed concerns def create_circle_button_click(self): # Mixed UI and business logic center = self.center_entry.get() radius = self.radius_entry.get() # Business logic mixed with UI acad_app = win32com.client.Dispatch("AutoCAD.Application") # ... more AutoCAD code mixed in self.status_label.config(text="Created circle")

principle.name: Use Threading for AutoCAD Operations
principle.description: Never block the UI thread with AutoCAD COM operations
principle.rationale: Prevents UI freezing and provides responsive user experience

example.bad: def on_button_click(self): """This will freeze the UI.""" # Direct AutoCAD call - blocks UI thread self.create_autocad_geometry() # UI freezes here self.status_var.set("Complete") # Never reached if above fails

principle.name: Implement Comprehensive Error Handling
principle.description: Handle all possible error conditions gracefully
principle.rationale: Provides robust applications and better user experience

example.bad: def unsafe_operation(self): """No error handling - application will crash.""" center = self.center_entry.get() radius = self.radius_entry.get() # No validation, no error handling result = self.acad_app.ActiveDocument.ModelSpace.AddCircle(center, radius) return result

convention.rule: Use descriptive names for Tkinter variables and methods
Organize code into logical sections with clear comments
Organize imports and use absolute imports
convention.good:
# Standard library imports import threading import queue import logging
# Third-party imports import tkinter as tk from tkinter import ttk import win32com.client import pythoncom
# Local imports from .autocad_manager import AutoCADManager from .validators import CoordinateValidator
convention.bad: # Unorganized imports import tkinter as tk, sys, os from tkinter import * import win32com.client as com

practice.description: Use grid system for complex layouts

guidelines.guideline: Plan your grid layout on paper first
Use columnconfigure and rowconfigure for proper expansion
Group related widgets in frames
Use consistent padding and spacing

practice.example:
def setup_main_layout(self): """Example of proper grid layout setup.""" # Configure main window self.root.columnconfigure(0, weight=1) self.root.rowconfigure(0, weight=1)
# Create main container main_frame = ttk.Frame(self.root, padding="10") main_frame.grid(row=0, column=0, sticky=(tk.W, tk.E, tk.N, tk.S))
# Configure main frame grid main_frame.columnconfigure(0, weight=1) main_frame.rowconfigure(1, weight=1) # Content area expands
# Header section header_frame = ttk.Frame(main_frame) header_frame.grid(row=0, column=0, sticky=(tk.W, tk.E), pady=(0, 10)) header_frame.columnconfigure(0, weight=1)
ttk.Label(header_frame, text="AutoCAD Geometry Tool", font=("Arial", 14, "bold")).grid(row=0, column=0)
# Content section content_frame = ttk.Frame(main_frame) content_frame.grid(row=1, column=0, sticky=(tk.W, tk.E, tk.N, tk.S)) content_frame.columnconfigure(0, weight=1) content_frame.rowconfigure(0, weight=1)
# Input section input_frame = ttk.LabelFrame(content_frame, text="Parameters", padding="5") input_frame.grid(row=0, column=0, sticky=(tk.W, tk.E), pady=(0, 10)) input_frame.columnconfigure(1, weight=1)
# Parameter inputs with proper grid layout ttk.Label(input_frame, text="Center X:").grid(row=0, column=0, sticky=tk.W, padx=(0, 5)) self.center_x_entry = ttk.Entry(input_frame) self.center_x_entry.grid(row=0, column=1, sticky=(tk.W, tk.E), padx=(0, 5))
ttk.Label(input_frame, text="Center Y:").grid(row=1, column=0, sticky=tk.W, padx=(0, 5)) self.center_y_entry = ttk.Entry(input_frame) self.center_y_entry.grid(row=1, column=1, sticky=(tk.W, tk.E), padx=(0, 5))

practice.description: Create layouts that adapt to window resizing

guidelines.guideline: Use weight > 0 for expandable columns/rows
Use sticky options for proper widget expansion
Bind to Configure event for dynamic layout changes
Test layouts at minimum and maximum window sizes

practice.example:
def make_layout_responsive(self): """Make layout responsive to window resizing."""
# Bind to window resize event self.root.bind('<Configure>', self.on_window_resize)
# Use relative sizing for widgets self.button_frame = ttk.Frame(self.main_frame) self.button_frame.grid(row=2, column=0, sticky=(tk.W, tk.E))
# Configure responsive columns for i in range(3): # Assuming 3 buttons self.button_frame.columnconfigure(i, weight=1)
# Create buttons that expand with container self.create_button = ttk.Button(self.button_frame, text="Create") self.create_button.grid(row=0, column=0, sticky=(tk.W, tk.E), padx=2)
self.cancel_button = ttk.Button(self.button_frame, text="Cancel") self.cancel_button.grid(row=0, column=1, sticky=(tk.W, tk.E), padx=2)
self.help_button = ttk.Button(self.button_frame, text="Help") self.help_button.grid(row=0, column=2, sticky=(tk.W, tk.E), padx=2)
def on_window_resize(self, event): """Handle window resize events.""" # Only respond to main window resize, not child widget events if event.widget == self.root: width = event.width height = event.height
# Adjust layout based on size if width < 600: # Compact layout self.switch_to_compact_layout() else: # Normal layout self.switch_to_normal_layout()

optimization.description: Proper memory management for COM objects

guidelines.guideline: Release COM objects explicitly when done
Use context managers for COM operations
Avoid keeping COM references longer than needed
Monitor memory usage in long-running applications

optimization.description: Efficient UI updates from background threads

guidelines.guideline: Use root.after() for thread-safe UI updates
Batch UI updates to reduce flicker
Use StringVar/DoubleVar for reactive updates
Avoid frequent UI updates during long operations

optimization.example:
class EfficientUIUpdater: """Efficient UI updates from background threads."""
def __init__(self, root): self.root = root self.pending_updates = {} self.update_lock = threading.Lock() self.update_scheduled = False
def schedule_ui_update(self, widget_method, *args, **kwargs): """Schedule UI update to be batched.""" with self.update_lock: key = (widget_method, args, kwargs) self.pending_updates[key] = True
if not self.update_scheduled: self.update_scheduled = True self.root.after(100, self.process_pending_updates) # Batch every 100ms
def process_pending_updates(self): """Process all pending UI updates.""" with self.update_lock: updates = list(self.pending_updates.keys()) self.pending_updates.clear() self.update_scheduled = False
# Execute all updates for widget_method, args, kwargs in updates: try: widget_method(*args, **kwargs) except Exception as e: print(f"UI update failed: {e}")
# Reschedule if more updates arrived during processing with self.update_lock: if self.pending_updates and not self.update_scheduled: self.update_scheduled = True self.root.after(100, self.process_pending_updates)
# Usage updater = EfficientUIUpdater(root)
def background_operation(): """Example background operation with efficient UI updates.""" for i in range(100): # Do work time.sleep(0.01)
# Schedule UI update (batched) updater.schedule_ui_update( self.progress_var.set, (i + 1) )
updater.schedule_ui_update( self.status_var.set, f"Processing: {i + 1}%" )
